title: 复习 · 第 1 期：我标过「不会」的词
objectives: 在 10 段完整短文里认出 102 个你标过「不会」的词
先靠上下文猜意思，再点词核对
重复出现的词多碰几次，加深印象

blocks.md:
这一节不教新词，只让你在**完整的短文**里反复碰到你标过「不会」的词。每段都是原创短文，仿《经济学人》《大西洋月刊》《科学美国人》《伦敦书评》等的笔法写的（真实文章有版权，不能原样搬）。

**读法**：先不点，按句子自己猜意思；猜不出来再点高亮的词看释义。同一个词会在不同段里重复出现，多碰几次自然就记住了。

blocks.text: The merger was announced with the [[nonchalant]] air of a routine reshuffle, yet the board's real purpose was hard to [[dissemble]]. A [[patchwork]] of regional units, each [[insular]] and faintly [[cliquish]], had long resisted head office's attempts to [[promulgate]] a single set of rules. When the chief executive tried to [[countermand]] a local decision, the [[vociferous]] objections from the field were so loud that she soon chose to [[annul]] her own order. The episode was a [[gaffe]], but a useful one: it showed how thin the firm's shared [[ethos]] had become, and how [[inimical]] to change its entrenched habits were.

gloss.nonchalant: 漫不经心的，若无其事的

blocks.text: For decades the standard account of the disease rested on a [[meager]] set of observations. Researchers, [[circumspect]] by training, hesitated to [[extrapolate]] from a handful of patients to a whole population, and the field stayed [[murky]]. Then an [[anomalous]] result changed matters: a group whose symptoms ought to have been mild instead showed signs of an [[impending]] collapse in immune function. The finding was [[nebulous]] at first, easy to dismiss as noise, but the team did not [[balk]]. Over three years the scattered clues [[coalesced|coalesce]] into a pattern, and the [[prognosis]] for such patients is now far less grim.

The poet's [[penchant]] for the [[bohemian]] life was [[congruent]] with his public image, though his letters reveal a more [[assiduous]] and [[austere]] worker than the legend allows. Early critics would [[extolled|extol]] him as a wild genius; later ones [[castigated|castigate]] him as a poseur. His [[diatribe]] against the academy, long taken as sincere, now reads as [[parody]], and a little [[disingenuous]]: he craved the [[approbation]] of the very professors he mocked.

gloss.parody: (以嘲笑原作作者的)模仿作品，恶搞

blocks.text: The new principal was [[imperious]] and, to many parents, [[tactless]]. Her rules were [[draconian]]: the handbook [[stipulated|stipulate]] everything from the length of skirts to the volume of laughter. Students, [[irascible]] at the best of times, produced a [[plethora]] of complaints, and soon a [[boisterous]] crowd filled the assembly hall. One [[intrepid]] teacher volunteered to [[adjudicate]] between the two sides, to the [[chagrin]] of a board that had hoped the quarrel would quietly go away.

gloss.chagrin: (因为失败、出糗而导致的)不安，焦虑

blocks.text: Along the [[brook]] the forest floor is a quiet economy of [[detritus]]. A [[copious]] fall of leaves each autumn feeds fungi, and the fungi feed larvae so [[minuscule]] that they escape notice until they [[metamorphose]] into [[gossamer]]-winged adults. [[Rapacious|rapacious]] beetles hunt the larvae, [[peripatetic]] herons pick off the beetles, and in a good year, a [[halcyon]] stretch of warm weather, nothing seems in [[dearth]]. A dry summer is another matter: so delicate a web of life can [[founder]] quickly.

At twenty she was a [[neophyte]] in a kitchen run by a [[truculent]] chef who treated every [[tyro]] as a personal insult. He would [[snub]] a cook for a bent knife, [[badger]] another about the salt, and [[chide]] the whole line whenever a sauce turned [[turbid]]. She learned to be [[circumspect]] with him, [[assiduous]] at her station and [[pensive]] on the long bus ride home, wondering whether any of it was worth the burns.

Fiscal rules are only as strong as the will to enforce them. A minister who can [[obviate]] a spending ceiling by declaring an emergency has merely dressed a [[discretionary]] choice up as a law. Such [[ad hoc]] exemptions are tempting when [[exigent]] circumstances arise, and money, being [[fungible]], quietly flows to favoured projects. Auditors may hint at [[malfeasance]], but without [[substantive]] powers they can only [[admonish]]; and a [[retroactive]] penalty raises its own questions of [[propriety]]. The rules, in short, [[hamstring]] only those who obey them.

Humans are [[credulous]] creatures, and a [[specious]] argument delivered with confidence will often beat a [[veracious]] one delivered with doubt. The [[knotty]] questions of ethics are rarely settled by those who [[prevaricate]] or by those who [[gainsay]] every objection; they are settled, if at all, by a [[tortuous]] process in which each side must [[concede]] something. Most of us, tired, will simply [[acquiesce]]. The [[invidious]] result is that the loudest voice, not the best-argued case, shapes the common view.

In the nineteenth century doctors would send the [[lethargic]] and the [[overwrought]] to mountain sanatoria, prescribing a [[salubrious]] climate and a [[temperate]] diet. The cure proved [[efficacious]] for some and, for others, a [[boon]] chiefly to the hotel owners. Families long [[beset]] by a relative's complaints finally found peace, while patients lay [[impassive]] on balconies and a fretful physician tried to [[attune]] the regimen to each case, hoping the thin air would prove [[conducive]] to rest.

gloss.lethargic: 没精打采的，行动迟缓的
gloss.overwrought: 十分激动的，非常不安的

blocks.md: ### 10. 注意力过剩的年代（媒体）

blocks.text: The cable networks face a [[glut]] of outrage and a shortage of attention. A [[lurid]] headline can still draw a crowd, but audiences have grown [[querulous]] about being shouted at. Politicians, once content to [[fawn]] over any host who would have them, now [[soft-pedal]] their harshest lines; the [[cavalier]] insult that won applause a decade ago invites [[censure]] today. The old strategy has become [[untenable]], and the [[laconic]] candidate, who says little and means it, has come to look refreshing.

gloss.untenable: 防守不住的，站不住脚的
gloss.laconic: 简洁(以至于显得粗鲁或难以理解)的

options: (因为失败、出糗而导致的)不安，焦虑
questions.explain: gaffe：（社交上的）失礼，失态，失言，出洋相（an embarrassing social blunder）。近义词：blunder, faux pas。
fungible：可互换的，可替代的（货物、财产等）（interchangeable with others of the same kind）。近义词：interchangeable, exchangeable。

questions.q: 哪个词的意思是「有效的」？
questions.explain: efficacious：有效的，灵验的（尤指药物、方法）（producing the desired effect）。

questions.q: 哪个词和 **sensational** 的意思最接近？
questions.explain: lurid 与 sensational 近义：shocking and sensational; glaringly bright。

questions.q:
选最适合填入空格的词：

> Fiscal rules are only as strong as the will to enforce them. A minister who can obviate a spending ceiling by declaring an emergency has merely dressed a discretionary choice up as a law. Such ad hoc exemptions are tempting when exigent circumstances arise, and money, being fungible, quietly flows to favoured projects. Auditors may hint at malfeasance, but without substantive powers they can only admonish; and a ____ penalty raises its own questions of propriety. The rules, in short, hamstring only those who obey them.
questions.explain: retroactive：有追溯效力的，溯及既往的（taking effect from a past date）。
